trial_court: Additional District & Sessions Judge, Fast Track, First Court, Suri, Birbhum, Rampurhat in Sessions Trial No. 2 October 2002 and Sessions Case No. 102 of 2002
case_name: Baidyanath Das @ Bedi And Others vs The State Of West Bengal

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Baidyanath Das @ Bedi and Others (husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law)

facts_of_case: Smt. Jharna Byen was married to Dilip Bayen for six years. Her husband, father-in-law, and mother-in-law started torturing her physically and mentally. She died by hanging herself at her in-laws' house due to continuous torture.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
legal_principles.held: It is settled law that the burden lies on the prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

legal_principles.principle: The testimony of a hostile witness is not reliable and should be viewed with skepticism.
legal_principles.held: However, it appears from his cross-examination that the accused persons arranged for medical treatment for her not giving birth to any child. Doctor never gave any final opinion that Jharna will never conceive.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's judgment and order of conviction were set aside, and the appeal was allowed.

use_for_drafting: drafting appeal against conviction for murder
